# Angle

[Framework](README.md) · `DotGame.Framework` · struct

```csharp
public readonly struct Angle : IEquatable<Angle>
```

An angle, stored in radians. It keeps degrees and radians apart: make one with [`FromDegrees`](#fromdegrees) or [`FromRadians`](#fromradians), and read it with [`Degrees`](#degrees) or [`Radians`](#radians).

## Remarks

It's an amount, not a direction, so `==` and `<` compare amounts: 360 degrees isn't equal to 0. Use [`Wrap`](#wrap) to compare directions, allowing for the rounding of floats.

## Methods

### FromDegrees

```csharp

```

Makes an angle from degrees.

### FromRadians

```csharp
public static Angle FromRadians(float radians)
```

Makes an angle from radians.

### FromVector

```csharp
public static Angle FromVector(Vector2 vector)
```

The direction of a vector: 0 points along positive X, and a positive angle turns toward positive Y, which is clockwise on screen. A zero vector gives 0.

### Lerp

```csharp
public static Angle Lerp(Angle from, Angle to, float amount)
```

Gets the angle partway between two angles, the shortest way round: from 350 to 10 degrees goes through 360. An amount outside 0 to 1 overshoots, which is meaningful for an angle. For a spin of more than half a turn, use `from + ((to - from) * amount)`.

### ToVector

```csharp
public Vector2 ToVector()
```

Gets the unit vector pointing at this angle, the inverse of [`FromVector`](#fromvector).

### Wrap

```csharp
public static Angle Wrap(Angle angle)
```

The same direction, with its value brought above -180 degrees and up to 180.
